# /choose-channels

The final step of the daily loop, F4, reached from `/write` or `/record`.
A person picks one or more of their own channels (Personal Archive, Family,
or other walls) and submits. This is where the entire loop's actual work
happens: the submit-to-unlock API call fires here, nowhere else in the
flow.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Route | `/choose-channels` |
| Router file | `app/choose-channels.tsx` |
| Flows | F4 Daily create and submit |
| Position in flow | step 4 of 5, the submit step |
| Data calls | one write, `dataClient.submit()` -> `POST /submit`, plus a read of the person's walls |
| Shared surface | none; the only screen in this flow that calls submit |

Cited to hs2studio/scribl-app at `c1b3c2d` on `main`, clean tree.

## Features

| Feature | Where it lives |
|---------|----------------|
| List the person's own channels/walls to choose among | `app/choose-channels.tsx:35`, `:42-44`, rendered `:134-158` |
| Multi-select any number of channels | `app/choose-channels.tsx:38`, `:54-64` |
| Skip the picker entirely on a pinned-prompt deep link, showing a one-wall confirmation instead | `app/choose-channels.tsx:121-132` |
| Submit the drawing plus caption-or-audio to the chosen channel(s) | `app/choose-channels.tsx:66-114` |
| Disable submit until at least one channel is picked (or the prompt is pinned) | `app/choose-channels.tsx:170` |
| Show a submit error inline without losing the picker state | `app/choose-channels.tsx:161-163` |
| Advance the client-side streak on a successful submit, fire-and-forget | `app/choose-channels.tsx:92` |
| Collapse the navigation stack after submit so back from the unlocked wall goes home, not back into the create flow | `app/choose-channels.tsx:98-107` |
| Back to `/story-select` | `app/choose-channels.tsx:119` |

There is no client-side membership gating on which channels appear or can
be chosen -- the comment at `app/choose-channels.tsx:25` states this
explicitly: AC2 (submit-to-unlock) and AC4 (membership) are enforced
server-side, this screen only calls the API and relays failures.

## Data calls

**One write, the consequential one.**

| Client method | Endpoint | Handler |
|---------------|----------|---------|
| `dataClient.submit()` | `POST /submit` | `backend/lambda/handlers/submit.ts` |

The client method is `src/data/http.ts:162-171` (the active client is
selected by `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE`, `src/data/index.ts:10-19`; the mock
adapter's own `submit()` is a separate implementation not read here). The
call site is `app/choose-channels.tsx:76-88`, inside `handleSubmit()`.

The request body assembles the whole draft:

```
promptId: draft.promptId
channelIds: pinnedChannelId ? [pinnedChannelId] : Array.from(selected)
imageRef: draft.imageRef
text: draft.audioRef ? undefined : draft.caption
audioRef: draft.audioRef
audioMime / audioDurationMs: set only when audioRef is set
strokes: serialized only if draft.strokes is non-null
```

(`app/choose-channels.tsx:71-87`). The `text`-vs-`audioRef` exclusion is
belt-and-braces here (the comment at `:80-82` calls it out): `useDraftStore`'s
`setCaption`/`setAudio` already make the two mutually exclusive at write
time, and the server's own CHECK constraint is the real guarantee
(`backend/lambda/handlers/submit.ts:61-70` rejects a request carrying both
with a 400 rather than letting the DB throw a 500).

**Server side.** `backend/lambda/handlers/submit.ts` validates `promptId`
and a non-empty `channelIds` array (`:24-35`), rejects text+audio together
(`:64-70`), writes the submission keyed by `(userId, promptId)` via
`putSubmission()` (`:97`, `:4`), and fires an un-awaited background
enhancement trigger per response id if AI enhancement is enabled and an
image was submitted (`:99-106`). The doc comment at the top of the file
(`:1-8`) states this is the ONLY write path that creates the submission row
the AC2 EXISTS check on the wall-read side depends on -- this is, by the
file's own account, the single point that unlocks the wall.

**Also reads walls.** `useWallsStore`'s `load()` populates the picker
(`app/choose-channels.tsx:35`, `:42-44`); its own client call is out of
scope for this page.

## State in, state out

**Reads on entry.** The full `useDraftStore` state via the `draft` hook
(`app/choose-channels.tsx:36`), and `walls` from `useWallsStore`
(`app/choose-channels.tsx:35`, loaded on mount at `:42-44`).

**R6 draft guard.** Mount-only, read via `getState()` specifically so
clearing the draft on a successful submit does not re-trigger the guard and
bounce the user off the wall they just unlocked (the code comment at
`:46-48` makes this reasoning explicit):

```
useEffect(() => {
  if (!useDraftStore.getState().imageRef) router.replace("/draw");
}, []);
```

at `app/choose-channels.tsx:49-52`.

**Writes on exit.** On success: `useDraftStore.getState().clearDraft()`
(`app/choose-channels.tsx:96`), then the R5 post-submit navigation
normalization -- `router.dismissAll()`, `router.replace("/home")`,
`router.push` to `/family` with the unlocked channel and prompt id
(`app/choose-channels.tsx:104-107`) -- so the back stack afterward is
exactly `[home, family]`, never back into `choose-channels`/`write`/`draw`.
On failure: nothing is cleared; `submitError` is set and the picker state
survives so the person can retry (`app/choose-channels.tsx:108-113`).

## Notes for planning

Authored here, not read out of the app.

### This is the one call in the whole app that unlocks a wall, and it has no idempotency guard visible from the client

`submit.ts`'s own comment calls this the only write path that creates the
row the AC2 EXISTS check depends on (`backend/lambda/handlers/submit.ts:1-8`).
The submission id is deterministic, `submission-${userId}-${promptId}`
(`:84`), which reads as an intentional idempotency key -- a double-tap or a
retried request for the same user and prompt should not create two rows.
But nothing on the client side (`app/choose-channels.tsx`) protects against
a double submit beyond the `submitting` boolean disabling the button
mid-flight (`:170`); a second tap that lands between render and disable, or
a retried request after a slow response the user thinks failed, is not
visibly guarded against from this file alone. Worth confirming the id
collision actually behaves as an upsert rather than a duplicate-key error
on the data layer this page did not open.

### The fan-out picker has no minimum-context UI for "why these walls"

The unpinned picker lists every wall the person belongs to with no
grouping, description, or indication of which one is the default/most-used
(`app/choose-channels.tsx:134-158`). For a person with more than a
Personal Archive and one Family wall, this screen offers no way to tell them
apart beyond the name. Not a defect in what shipped, since the POC's wall
count is small, but a first thing to reconsider once wall count grows.

### The pinned path and the fan-out path share one submit call, and that is the right call

Worth stating positively rather than just as a fact: the C15 pinned-prompt
path (submitting to one specific wall from an injected prompt) and the
ordinary daily-prompt fan-out both resolve to the exact same
`dataClient.submit()` invocation with a one-element `channelIds` array
(`app/choose-channels.tsx:71`, `:121-132`). There is exactly one submit code
path in this screen, not two parallel ones that could drift apart.
